evidence.observation: Library-level search/replace primitive used by the flexible edit strategies. It counts occurrences of search_text in original_text and returns None when num == 0 (no match), but the uniqueness guard `if num > 1: raise SearchTextNotUnique()` is commented out at lines 438-439, so it currently falls through to original_text.replace(search_text, replace_text) and rewrites every occurrence. This is the ambiguity contract marker the edit-block failure case is the analogue of: ambiguity must be refused, not silently applied to an arbitrary/all locations.

`class SearchTextNotUnique(ValueError)` is the designated ambiguity-failure signal of the search/replace engine. It is imported and caught by aider/coders/udiff_coder.py (lines 8, 95, 276), where a caught SearchTextNotUnique converts the hunk into a user-facing 'not unique' error. It establishes that an ambiguous SEARCH match is a failure condition in this repository's contract, which is exactly the behaviour the new edit-block test pins.

Elided (`...`) SEARCH/REPLACE handling. For each non-empty `...`-delimited piece it raises ValueError when the piece does not occur in whole (line 233-234) and, crucially, when whole.count(part) > 1 (lines 235-236). This is the explicit ambiguous-match rejection inside edit-block handling. Its caller replace_most_similar_chunk wraps the call in try/except ValueError and returns None (lines 176-181), so an ambiguous elided search fails the whole block instead of editing an arbitrary occurrence.

The newly added focused ambiguous-match failure case. It feeds an elided SEARCH block whose pieces (`aaa`, `bbb`) each appear twice to eb.replace_most_similar_chunk and asserts the result is None (edit rejected, no wrong-location edit), then asserts the identical edit returns the expected replaced text when each piece is unique. This is the executable contract for the ambiguous-match failure path.

Pre-existing contrast case documenting the other half of the ambiguity contract: a plain (non-elided) SEARCH that matches `line1` twice deterministically replaces only the FIRST occurrence and returns the edited text (not None). Together with the new test this pins the full contract — plain ambiguity resolves to the first occurrence, whereas elided (`...`) ambiguity with duplicated pieces is refused with None.

claims.claim: `aider/coders/search_replace.py` defines the ambiguity failure signal `SearchTextNotUnique(ValueError)` and its `search_and_replace` primitive counts matches (returning None for zero matches) while leaving the `num > 1` uniqueness guard commented out, so the module itself is the source of the repository's ambiguous-match contract that edit-block handling mirrors.

`tests/basic/test_editblock.py` now contains a focused ambiguous-match failure case (`test_replace_most_similar_chunk_ambiguous_dotdotdots_fails`) that asserts `eb.replace_most_similar_chunk` returns None when an elided SEARCH piece matches more than once, and returns the correctly-edited text when each piece is unique; the pre-existing `test_replace_multiple_matches` documents the contrasting first-occurrence rule for plain (non-elided) ambiguous matches.

The ambiguous-match failure is enforced inside edit-block handling by `try_dotdotdots`, which raises ValueError when `whole.count(part) > 1`; `replace_most_similar_chunk` catches that ValueError and returns None, so an ambiguous elided edit is rejected rather than applied to an arbitrary occurrence, matching the new test's expectation.

conclusion: An ambiguous SEARCH match is a failure condition in aider's edit-block handling, not a guess. The minimal, focused addition is a single test method in tests/basic/test_editblock.py (test_replace_most_similar_chunk_ambiguous_dotdotdots_fails, lines 300-321) that pins the elided-`...` ambiguity path: duplicated SEARCH pieces make replace_most_similar_chunk return None (rejected), while the identical edit succeeds when the pieces are unique. This is the concrete analogue of the library-level SearchTextNotUnique(ValueError) signal in aider/coders/search_replace.py; the contrasting first-occurrence rule for plain ambiguity (test_replace_multiple_matches) is left unchanged.
